title: How far is as far as it gets?
hook: Pick any spot. How far away can the other side of the world be?

knows: the Earth's circumference is about 40,000 km
doesNotKnow: the largest possible distance between two places
that the farthest place from you is a single point

misconception: Two places on Earth can be as far apart as the Earth's circumference, 40,000 km.
objective: The learner can say that no two places are more than about 20,000 km apart, and that the farthest place from you is one point, your antipode.

claims.text: Half way round the Earth is 20,015 km on a sphere, and no two places are farther apart.
claims.source: pi x R with R = 6,371.0088 km (IUGG mean radius) = 20,015.1 km (node: Math.PI * 6371.0088, builder's scratch script). On the real, slightly flattened Earth the maximum is about 20,004 km (brief; from memory, not displayed). The lesson labels the stage 'Sphere model'.

claims.text: Only one place is that far from you: the point opposite you, your antipode.
claims.source: On a sphere the only point at distance pi R is the antipode.

claims.text: The edge of the azimuthal equidistant map is the single antipode point stretched into a circle.
claims.source: Snyder (1987), Map Projections: A Working Manual, ch. 25 (cited from memory): in the azimuthal equidistant projection the antipode of the centre is the whole bounding circle.

claims.text: A ring drawn 20,000 km from the pin is only about 95 km long on the Earth.
claims.source: Ring length 2 pi R sin(d/R) at d = 20,000 km = 95 km (node, scratch script; 5,000 km gives 28,289 km, 10,008 km gives the 40,030 km maximum).

claims.text: Madrid to Wellington is 19,855 km (shortest way).
claims.source: d3-geo geoDistance x 6,371.0088 km, Madrid 40.4168 N 3.7038 W, Wellington 41.2865 S 174.7762 E (coordinates from memory of a gazetteer): 19,854.8 km.

claims.text: Distances measured from the pin are true on this map.
claims.source: Snyder (1987) ch. 25 (from memory): azimuthal equidistant preserves distance from the centre; distances between other pairs are not preserved.

recall.question: Which is the farthest any two places on Earth can be apart, going the shortest way?
options: About 40,000 km, all the way round
It depends which two places you pick, with no limit
recall.why: The shortest path never goes more than half way round; the farthest point from you is your antipode, about 20,000 km away.
